episodes.secret: The gas-main pressure chart shows exactly three erased inspections and a handwritten initials mark from Dez's former boss.
episodes.relationship: A neighborhood cook offers testimony only if the displaced kitchen staff will still have jobs afterward.
episodes.betrayal: His former boss proposes torching the inspection originals to spare the workers a public scandal.
episodes.fallout: The city's restaurants must decide whether the person who saved their kitchens gets to control their safety forever.

episodes.secret: A lightning-rod repair tag bears the airfield owner's signature, but the replacement was installed a week after Pip fell.
episodes.relationship: A grounded air-traffic controller promises to stay on the runway while Pip attempts her first real landing.
episodes.betrayal: The airfield insurer will erase Pip's pilot record if she accuses the owner publicly.
episodes.fallout: Keeping airspace safe now means trusting somebody else to hold the emergency controls while she lands.

episodes.secret: The transcript proves rescuers were ordered to stop drilling on day six, when Tug was still tapping a rescue rhythm below.
episodes.relationship: A retired tunnel worker asks Tug to march beside families whose loved ones were never found.
episodes.betrayal: A contractor offers him the original digging maps if he agrees to collapse the evidence vault after reading them.
episodes.fallout: The hospital district stands on the same hollow foundations; exposing one crime could open another sinkhole.

episodes.secret: Marisol finds a filtration report recording poisonous discharge on the very day the power company declared the pond safe.
episodes.relationship: A harbor diver asks for a shared rescue instead of another lone feat that makes the dock workers invisible.
episodes.betrayal: The company offers free desalination for her family's neighborhood in exchange for one falsified water sample.
episodes.fallout: The harbor needs clean water long after any television crew leaves, even if the responsible directors remain wealthy.

episodes.secret: Kenji discovers the metal fragment's telemetry matches a classified training satellite built to predict human movement.
episodes.relationship: An exhausted martial arts instructor asks Kenji to demonstrate restraint in front of the cadets who idolize him.
episodes.betrayal: The defense contractor offers to return his teacher's lost certification if Kenji destroys the surviving telemetry.
episodes.fallout: He must decide whether perfectly controlled movement can become a public skill rather than another private weapon.

episodes.secret: Otto finds the sludge formula in a discarded student refrigerator, annotated by a pharmaceutical intern who later disappeared.
episodes.relationship: A fellow laboratory technician needs her to publish the failed trials without stealing credit for the intern's discovery.
episodes.betrayal: The lab promises the intern a settlement if Otto signs a patent assignment that hides the risks.
episodes.fallout: Her breakthrough could cure hundreds, but only if the people exposed to it are allowed to decide its use.

episodes.secret: Gus discovers the cape's activation log contains a remote command issued from inside the Valcourt family dining room.
episodes.relationship: A family driver tells Gus what the estate staff sacrificed to keep the old hero legend spotless.
episodes.betrayal: A cousin offers an invitation to the family trust board in return for blaming the lightning on a dead servant.
episodes.fallout: The Valcourt name will survive graduation; the question is who has a right to shelter beneath it.

episodes.secret: Fen recovers a live mixing-board recording proving someone boosted the rooftop broadcast past every safety limit.
episodes.relationship: A busker who lost their hearing at that show wants the audience to hear their story, not Fen's hit single.
episodes.betrayal: A talent manager offers Fen a stadium tour if the original neighborhood performers waive their claims.
episodes.fallout: The city can sing together again only when the overlooked chorus chooses to participate.

episodes.secret: Ruby finds a registration transcript with a blank section labeled the memory the state extracted without permission.
episodes.relationship: A former records clerk asks her to protect the other young mutants whose memories were filed as property.
episodes.betrayal: The registrar offers Ruby her own missing memory if she helps burn the records of twenty others.
episodes.fallout: A private identity cannot be reclaimed by selling every other person's right to remember.

episodes.secret: Corvin follows a feather sale to a couture warehouse where captive mutants are cataloged as rare livestock.
episodes.relationship: A winged rescue volunteer refuses to be photographed and asks Corvin to make the victims the authors of their own escape.
episodes.betrayal: The fashion house offers to sponsor protective housing if Corvin keeps its donor list confidential.
episodes.fallout: The freedom to fly must belong to people who cannot afford a designer costume.

episodes.secret: Hattie discovers a childhood seismic monitor stitched into the floorboards of her family's old apartment.
episodes.relationship: A community geologist believes her footsteps predicted danger, not the disaster the city accused her of causing.
episodes.betrayal: A developer offers to name a new park after her if she allows a hidden fault line to stay unmapped.
episodes.fallout: Residents must choose whether to confront a real earthquake warning or preserve the value of their homes.

episodes.secret: Ilya tracks dead fish back to a factory outlet hidden under a seafood distributor's loading dock.
episodes.relationship: A fishing crew invites Ilya aboard only if he stops assuming he alone can heal the whole bay.
episodes.betrayal: The distributor offers to save his family's boat if he agrees that the poisoning was natural.
episodes.fallout: The harbor's recovery belongs to the crews who endured the poisoned seasons, not to its newest mascot.

episodes.secret: Asha finds decades of visitor logs showing that academy recruiters watched her grandmother's dance classes in secret.
episodes.relationship: A dancer asks Asha to teach the techniques without turning the dancers into a military talent pipeline.
episodes.betrayal: A recruiter promises to protect her grandmother's school if Asha names the most gifted children.
episodes.fallout: Her family's movements were never an admission ticket the academy owned.

episodes.secret: Theo obtains the sale ledger for their brain scans and recognizes the signature of a physician they once trusted.
episodes.relationship: A classmate offers to sit through Theo's headaches while the two decide what information is safe to publish.
episodes.betrayal: A researcher offers to halt the growth if Theo agrees to model the city's citizens as predictable assets.
episodes.fallout: Theo cannot forecast the value of love or loyalty by treating everyone as a data point.

episodes.secret: Seraphine finds an entire wing of family portraits painted over where past guardians refused their assigned role.
episodes.relationship: An elderly guardian who walked away offers her shelter without demanding another oath.
episodes.betrayal: The family matriarch offers to restore her mother's reputation if Seraphine erases the dissenting portraits.
episodes.fallout: The next generation deserves a choice about whose wings keep watch over them.

episodes.secret: Lucky finds the fire-station note in the same handwriting as confidential donor files that map the city's charitable favors.
episodes.relationship: A foster sibling asks him for friendship without another extraordinary favor they can never repay.
episodes.betrayal: A benefactor promises to reveal his parents if Lucky agrees to bind the orphanage to their political campaign.
episodes.fallout: Affection freely chosen carries more weight than any gift extracted through a superpower.

episodes.secret: Vee proves that an insurer's fire-risk algorithm targeted buildings immediately before its investors bought the land.
episodes.relationship: A displaced tenant organizer asks Vee to teach ordinary residents how to maintain the safety system.
episodes.betrayal: A landlord offers to protect her family's rent if she falsifies one crucial sensor reading.
episodes.fallout: Every apartment saved is evidence that public safety cannot be sold back to the people paying for it.

episodes.secret: Jun-ho uncovers wingsuit patents assigned to the buyer before the complaint that ended his airfield career.
episodes.relationship: A volunteer flight medic asks him to redesign his glider for carrying patients instead of racing sponsors.
episodes.betrayal: The buyer offers him his pilot license back for sabotaging a rival emergency air corridor.
episodes.fallout: The skyline will remember whether he opened a rescue route or claimed its airspace.

episodes.secret: Delphine extracts a sample showing a municipal tower used decorative steel instead of the promised structural reinforcement.
episodes.relationship: A construction forewoman wants to testify beside Delphine, not hide behind her armor during the hearing.
episodes.betrayal: A planning official offers to save a low-income housing block if Delphine condemns the next block instead.
episodes.fallout: It is easy to build a monument; harder to build a city people can afford to remain in.

episodes.secret: Nalani discovers records showing rescue boats were transferred to a yacht club the day before the coastal storm.
episodes.relationship: A coast guard mechanic asks for an open repair manual so fishers can fix their own emergency vessels.
episodes.betrayal: The captain offers a restored boat to Nalani's family if she signs a false salvage report.
episodes.fallout: Survival at sea cannot depend on whether a person can afford a member's berth.

episodes.secret: Marcus finds the safety officer's original training-accident video, with a missing thirty-second interval.
episodes.relationship: A trainee who suffered the same injury asks Marcus to support a safer program instead of winning a grudge match.
episodes.betrayal: The academy offers to restore Marcus's medals if he testifies that his injured teammates disobeyed orders.
episodes.fallout: The perfect drill is worthless if the people running it are treated as replaceable.

episodes.secret: Lionel's stolen F.R.O.G. leap-gear patent includes a lab addendum proving the enhancement serum causes progressive amphibian mutations. The dean approved the research only after striking out the human-consent clause.
episodes.relationship: Ada Glass, the chemist who caught the error, invites Lionel to demonstrate his human-powered rescue rig at the hospital. She will not sign the experimental serum waiver, no matter what he promises.
episodes.betrayal: The institute offers Lionel an exclusive hero license if he injects the serum and lets the company hide evidence of the test subjects. His brilliant human mind might survive; his human body will not.
episodes.fallout: Dr. Frog must choose between being a human inventor responsible to patients and an amphibian genius who decides their evolution for them. The leap harness was enough to save lives all along.

episodes.secret: Bart follows a crate of Sterling weapons from the family factory directly into a gang-owned warehouse.
episodes.relationship: A whistleblower engineer asks him to protect their family rather than stage a flashy shareholder rebellion.
episodes.betrayal: His father offers Bart control of the company if he lets the next shipment cross the river.
episodes.fallout: Inheritance is a tool for restitution or control, but never an excuse to avert your eyes.

episodes.secret: Dani discovers the protester identity leak originated from an account impersonating the volunteer moderation team.
episodes.relationship: A former protest leader will cooperate only if Dani allows them to speak without an algorithm selecting their words.
episodes.betrayal: A sponsor offers to restore Dani's public reputation by posting forged evidence against the leaker.
episodes.fallout: Truth is more than a trend, especially when a frightened witness cannot safely go viral.

episodes.secret: Hollis learns the salamander has been held inside the candle through seven generations of family bargains.
episodes.relationship: A firekeeper asks Hollis to negotiate with the creature as a person rather than use it as a spell component.
episodes.betrayal: A coven offers to release the salamander if Hollis permanently binds another living flame in its place.
episodes.fallout: The oldest bargain is not sacred merely because nobody has dared ask the flame for consent.

episodes.secret: Ambrose finds a library stamp in the cursed wind book that predates the building by two hundred years.
episodes.relationship: A librarian asks him to return the stolen pages before the storm erases the memories trapped in the margins.
episodes.betrayal: A collector offers to restore Ambrose's lost songs if he blames the book's author for the approaching gale.
episodes.fallout: Stories carried on the wind still belong to the people who lived them.

episodes.secret: An old tenant deed sewn inside Granny Mayhem's quilt names the harbor boarding house as a protected community shelter. A city land broker had the ownership records erased before the demolition order.
episodes.relationship: Etta Brooks, the tenant-council chair, invites Mavis to dinner but insists Granny stop speaking for every resident. Love and loyalty cannot be substituted for a neighborhood vote.
episodes.betrayal: A broker promises to protect Granny's grown children if she stitches all of Comet City into a locked, obedient quilt neighborhood. Her knitting needles are already binding doors before she chooses.
episodes.fallout: Granny Mayhem can hand her rune needles to the tenants and become their wildest defender, or keep them and turn a city's entire population into her captive family.

episodes.secret: Caspian sees a drowned stranger in the mirror-bowl and realizes the pawnbroker has sold the same vision before.
episodes.relationship: A water-diviner asks him to hear survivors' accounts instead of treating every reflection as prophecy.
episodes.betrayal: The pawnbroker promises Caspian the future he wants if he delivers the bowl to a new victim.
episodes.fallout: A reflection is a possible future, not permission to choose a stranger's fate.

episodes.secret: Ada discovers the monastery's refugee denial was paid for with a land deed signed in her own teacher's hand.
episodes.relationship: A former novice asks her to open the gate to displaced families without demanding conversion or gratitude.
episodes.betrayal: The order offers to restore her rank if she publicly denounces the people it locked outside.
episodes.fallout: Discipline means protecting vulnerable people when tradition has failed its own vows.

episodes.secret: Lucan finds his professor's handwriting in the margins of an equation she publicly claimed to invent.
episodes.relationship: A doctoral student who still admires the professor begs Lucan to expose the theft without erasing her from existence.
episodes.betrayal: The professor offers the missing proof if Lucan agrees to make her rival disappear instead.
episodes.fallout: An elegant proof is no excuse for treating a living person as a removable variable.

episodes.secret: Isadora finds her mother's missing diary page folded inside a hearth charm under the family floor.
episodes.relationship: A distant cousin asks to share their inherited spellbook instead of letting Isadora rule the entire coven.
episodes.betrayal: The coven elders offer to reveal her mother's whereabouts if she binds the younger witches to her authority.
episodes.fallout: Home is a place where someone can leave and still be loved, not a throne held together by secrets.

episodes.secret: Remy hears an old crossroads melody reveal the names of understudies who disappeared after accepting applause.
episodes.relationship: A stagehand asks Remy to give the forgotten performers their names back on opening night.
episodes.betrayal: The spirit offers him standing ovations forever if he transfers the contract to another actor.
episodes.fallout: The curtain can rise without anyone selling another soul to keep the audience watching.

episodes.secret: Ixi traces a faint distress flare to a colony escape pod held beneath a government energy laboratory.
episodes.relationship: A displaced alien parent asks her to organize transport for the whole family, not rescue only the pod containing her own.
episodes.betrayal: A scientist offers to return Ixi's records if she signs away the other pods as state property.
episodes.fallout: A new sun cannot be built from captives whose only crime was surviving the old one.

episodes.secret: Quillon finds a reopened rift that leads home for exactly thirteen seconds every lunar tide.
episodes.relationship: A local friend asks Quillon to be honest about leaving instead of promising a future they cannot keep.
episodes.betrayal: An ambassador offers permanent legal status if Quillon shuts the rift before the other refugees arrive.
episodes.fallout: A home is not a privilege that must be purchased by closing the road to everyone else.

episodes.secret: Kesh recognizes a family voice vibrating through a meteorite sculpture at a donor's private gallery.
episodes.relationship: A geologist asks Kesh to consult the surviving fragments before smashing what may be another sleeping person.
episodes.betrayal: The curator offers to assemble Kesh's kin if Kesh agrees to join the collection voluntarily.
episodes.fallout: An exhibition of living beings is still a prison even when the patrons call it preservation.

episodes.secret: Thessaly learns the whirlpool is a lifeboat beacon whose origin world may already have vanished.
episodes.relationship: A lighthouse keeper invites her to choose Comet City without pretending her lost ocean never existed.
episodes.betrayal: An oceanic syndicate offers to reopen the beacon in exchange for ownership of the harbor tides.
episodes.fallout: No one owns the sea just because they understand its current better than their neighbors.

episodes.secret: Zuzu's cracked portal compass contains a murder warrant signed by the same guild broker who built Comet City's hidden extradimensional transit registry. The named victim is an innocent refugee child.
episodes.relationship: Sable Fern offers Zuzu a place in her refugee household and asks him to explain his oath without the sword in his hand. He is invited as a person, not hired as protection.
episodes.betrayal: His old assassin guild offers safe passage home and a restored name if Zuzu completes one final execution. A black clockwork suit and forbidden portal keys arrive with the order.
episodes.fallout: Zuzu, Koala Assassin can cut the warrants and let refugees choose their own futures, or accept the portal keys and become a small, terrifying judge who can strike anyone between seconds.

episodes.secret: Oorin decodes an observation stream proving his civilization has been treating Earth as a social experiment.
episodes.relationship: A local research assistant asks him to acknowledge the people whose lives his home world's findings have damaged.
episodes.betrayal: His supervisor offers safe passage home if he conceals the ethics violations from Earth's citizens.
episodes.fallout: True discovery requires letting the people being studied decide whether the experiment continues.

episodes.secret: Ysolde finds a scratched mirror edge engraved with her foster mother's private lullaby from another universe.
episodes.relationship: A palace servant asks Ysolde to keep the refugee children safe before seeking her stolen throne.
episodes.betrayal: A regent offers the royal crown if she condemns her foster mother as an impostor.
episodes.fallout: A crown from one universe cannot erase the debts of love in the world that raised her.

episodes.secret: Pellanor discovers the crash beacon was deliberately severed from their collective just as a rescue fleet approached.
episodes.relationship: A solitary radio operator offers friendship that cannot be voted into existence by a chorus of minds.
episodes.betrayal: The collective offers instant reunion if Pellanor supplies its leaders with the city's private thoughts.
episodes.fallout: Belonging matters only when a dissenting voice may still say no.

episodes.secret: Cassidy discovers a second prescription label describing emotional ignition as a profitable treatment side effect.
episodes.relationship: A clinic counselor asks Cassidy to sit with survivors without trying to burn away their fear.
episodes.betrayal: The manufacturer offers a cure for Cassidy's pain if the trial patients are declared mentally unstable.
episodes.fallout: An honest flame can illuminate medical abuse without consuming the people living through it.

episodes.secret: Avery finds an old family photograph showing their grandmother hovering inches above a dance floor.
episodes.relationship: A relative asks Avery to tell their parents gently before the press turns family history into a conspiracy.
episodes.betrayal: A collector offers proof of the grandmother's powers if Avery agrees to steal her hospital file.
episodes.fallout: Flight is freedom, not the obligation to carry a family's secrets indefinitely.

episodes.secret: Rafa senses a witness trapped in the stone foundation of city hall, still repeating the date of a buried crime.
episodes.relationship: A community historian asks Rafa to protect living descendants rather than dramatize the old scandal.
episodes.betrayal: A councillor offers public exoneration if Rafa seals the confession back into the cornerstone.
episodes.fallout: A city built on stolen land must learn to hear the people under its monuments.

episodes.secret: Lior discovers his mother's medication was altered by a wellness clinic marketing borrowed happiness as treatment.
episodes.relationship: A nurse asks Lior to support his mother's own choices instead of absorbing every sadness she feels.
episodes.betrayal: The clinic promises relief from his emotional overload if he transfers his mother's grief into strangers.
episodes.fallout: Care is not the same as control, and love cannot substitute for another person's medical agency.

episodes.secret: Mei Lin finds the names of secret school graduates crossed out after the library's trustees signed a censorship contract.
episodes.relationship: A retired librarian asks her to restore the lost students' voices without turning their memories into a weapon.
episodes.betrayal: The trustees offer to reopen her training hall if she erases the last witness to the school purge.
episodes.fallout: Stillness can protect frightened people, but silence imposed by power is another kind of prison.

episodes.secret: Ezra finds an entrance-exam recording proving the person who sold him answers worked for the scholarship committee.
episodes.relationship: A classmate asks him to admit the cheating without inviting the academy to expel students who helped him study afterward.
episodes.betrayal: The committee offers Ezra an honors diploma if he falsely accuses the student who warned him.
episodes.fallout: Belonging begins when he can succeed in public without stealing anyone else's chance.

episodes.secret: Celestine discovers her own name in a prom disaster prophecy dated before the academy was built.
episodes.relationship: A dancer asks her to experience one ordinary evening without trying to script everyone else's tomorrow.
episodes.betrayal: A cult offers to prevent the vision if she engineers one smaller sacrifice before the last dance.
episodes.fallout: Foreknowledge is an invitation to change a future, not a license to punish people for a fate they never chose.

episodes.secret: Juniper traces the devastating leak to a trusted news editor who sold one witness's private grief to a campaign.
episodes.relationship: A friend agrees to share their secret only if Juniper promises not to turn it into a headline.
episodes.betrayal: The editor offers her a famous investigative column if she publishes an innocent source's identity.
episodes.fallout: Trust can survive a public confession, but not a secret transaction made with someone else's dignity.
